messages:
Priya Patel: Quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands about engineering process: release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs. Drop short Qs and we'll answer during the live Q&A.

Alex Chen: Are weekly release trains still the goal for hosted? saw a couple slips.

Priya Patel: Yes, weekly remains target for hosted. Slips were due to large infra migrations and a couple emergency rollbacks. We'll publish an exception policy with examples.

Samir Gupta: Canary length and rollback thresholds? do runtime-impacting PRs need full perf pre-merge?

Priya Patel: Default canary = 30m. Rollback if error rate >0.5% above baseline OR p95 latency +15% sustained 5m. Runtime PRs need smoke perf checks pre-merge; full perf suite runs post-merge and will block promotion for regressions. Use the "perf-test" PR label.

Marta Lopez: Any plan to move to 2-week oncall rotations? 1-week is tough.

Priya Patel: We'll pilot 2-week infra rotations next quarter. Runtime oncall stays 1-week for now. Coverage model: runtime = 1 primary + 1 secondary; infra = 1 primary + 2 secondaries. Rota + shadowing doc coming.

Alex Chen: Will Releases UI show per-route canary health (p50/p95/error-rate)?

Priya Patel: Yes, route-level p50/p95/error-rate and a canary health badge in Releases. Alex: please mock the UI and link in the doc.

Samir Gupta: Hosted SLA still 99.9? Dedicated higher tiers?

Priya Patel: Public hosted SLA target remains 99.9. Dedicated customers can opt into 99.95 with reserved capacity and contract. We'll publish an SLA matrix with examples next week.

Priya Patel: Action items: I'll draft a one-pager. @Marta Lopez to draft hosted vs dedicated release differences. @Alex Chen to mock console canary UI. Post PRs to #eng-docs and we'll iterate.
